newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finmin accepts real interest rate rise '97.
newsitem.headline: Polish finmin accepts real interest rate rise '97.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry does not object to the central bank's plan to allow real interest rates to rise in 1997, a deputy finance minister said on Wednesday.

Halina Wasilewska-Trenkner said the ministry agreed with the National Bank of Poland (NBP) that lowering real rates in line with falling inflation could overheat the economy, considering the recent rise of demand for credit.
"We cannot always say that it is good to reduce interest rates to catch up with falling inflation," she told a news conference.
"When demand for money is high...cutting the price of money could lead to overheating the economy," she added.
The NBP has said it was likely to allow its interest rates to rise in real terms to limit inflationary credit growth and cool down booming demand.
The bank's official lombard and discount rates are now 25 and 22 percent respectively while market rates are about 19.5 percent.
The government plans to cut inflation to 13 percent at the end of 1997 from 19.5 percent in October and about 18 percent projected for the end of this year.
